consensus_summary: A highway primarily symbolizes God’s prepared way of salvation, holiness, and restoration, especially the redeemed people’s return to God or Zion.
book_summary: The highway is the way of holiness, understood as the prepared road home.
consensus_core_identification: God’s prepared holy way for the redeemed to return.
boundary_disagreement: None material. The book selects the Isaiah 35 holiness-and-return strand that already stands at the center of the consensus; it simply omits other associated highway applications.
rationale: “The way of holiness” directly matches the consensus’s dominant identification from Isaiah 35:8, while “the prepared road home” corresponds to the widely recognized restoration and return-to-Zion dimension. The book’s brevity does not materially narrow or reclassify the symbol; it states the same core in compressed language.
strongest_objection: Isaiah 35:8 explicitly names the highway as “the way of holiness” but does not, in the isolated verse, explicitly say “home”; that nuance depends on the surrounding return-to-Zion context, especially verses 9–10. Even so, it does not create a substantive disagreement with the consensus.
